subject.title: fix(slack): bound one-shot WebClient/write timeouts without Bolt deadline

question: Should one-shot Slack web and write calls adopt fixed 30-second and 60-second defaults despite the possibility that a timed-out write was accepted remotely?
rationale: The patch is technically sound, but choosing when an external write becomes an ambiguous timeout is an operator and message-delivery policy decision that tests cannot settle.

options.title: Accept bounded defaults
options.body: Refresh the branch and land the 30-second web and 60-second write defaults while relying on existing reconciliation for ambiguous writes.

options.title: Revise the write policy
options.body: Keep the one-shot web deadline but adjust or defer the write deadline until the desired ambiguous-delivery recovery contract is explicit.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded defaults
recommendation.body: Refresh the branch and land the 30-second web and 60-second write defaults while relying on existing reconciliation for ambiguous writes.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged work established the shared Slack client-options boundary affected by this decision.
